definitions.explanation: The material forming the inner core of a layered or composite structure. Used in construction, manufacturing, and materials science to describe the central structural component.
The dense, dark inner wood of a tree trunk, as opposed to the lighter sapwood on the outside. Heartwood is valued in woodworking for its durability and color.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}の{芯材|しんざい}に{合板|ごうはん}を{使用|しよう}した。
examples.english: Plywood was used as the core material for the wall.

examples.japanese: この{断熱|だんねつ}パネルの{芯材|しんざい}は{発泡|はっぽう}ウレタンでできている。
examples.english: The core material of this insulation panel is made of urethane foam.

examples.japanese: {軽量|けいりょう}で{強度|きょうど}のある{芯材|しんざい}を{選|えら}ぶことが、サンドイッチ{構造|こうぞう}の{設計|せっけい}では{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: Choosing a lightweight yet strong core material is important in the design of sandwich structures.

examples.japanese: {檜|ひのき}の{芯材|しんざい}は{赤|あか}みがかっている。
examples.english: The heartwood of cypress has a reddish tint.

examples.japanese: {芯材|しんざい}は{辺材|へんざい}より{耐久性|たいきゅうせい}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: Heartwood is more durable than sapwood.

examples.japanese: {家具|かぐ}{職人|しょくにん}は{木目|もくめ}の{美|うつく}しい{芯材|しんざい}を{好|この}んで{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Furniture craftsmen prefer to use heartwood with beautiful grain patterns.

notes:
A compound of {芯|しん} (core) and {材|ざい} (material/wood). The word has two distinct domains: in manufacturing it means core material in a composite structure, and in forestry/woodworking it means the dark inner wood of a tree.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {芯材|しんざい}と{表面材|ひょうめんざい}: core and surface material
- {芯材|しんざい}と{辺材|へんざい}: heartwood and sapwood
- {断熱|だんねつ}{芯材|しんざい}: insulation core material

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {心材|しんざい}: heartwood (alternate kanji, same meaning in the forestry sense)
- {辺材|へんざい}: sapwood (the lighter outer wood, opposite of heartwood)
- {基材|きざい}: base material; substrate
